overview: After 1.e4 c5 White plays the king to e2 for no reason of development. It loses a tempo, blocks the f1 bishop and exposes the king in the centre. Black can develop freely with ...Nc6, ...e5 and ...d5, so it is a joke or surprise line.

white_ideas.idea: Follow with d4 or Nf3 and hope Black overreaches
Use the king step to avoid theory

black_ideas.idea: Hit the exposed king with ...d5 and ...Qb6 ideas

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian-like set-up with White king on e2

character.notes: No real fight; White simply has an awkward king.

soundness.notes: The king walk costs time and has no purpose.

structure.notes: A c5 pawn against e4, no pawn trades yet.

approach.notes: Chosen only as a joke or a surprise.

character.reason: It is neither known for tactics nor hard to break; the king move just wastes time.

soundness.reason: The king on e2 loses a tempo and blocks White development.

structure.reason: It remains a Sicilian pawn structure with the c-file for Black.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner.
